groups.title: Vue 3 Reactivity System
groups.question: A Vue component stops updating after destructuring a reactive object, and a watcher is used where a computed value would do. Explain Vue's reactivity tools.

followUps.ref vs reactive: Choosing the Right Prim: When would you use ref and when reactive?
followUps.computed vs watchEffect: Derived State: When would you use computed and when watchEffect?

evidence.text: ref wraps any value and is accessed through .value.
reactive makes an object deeply reactive.
Destructuring a reactive object loses reactivity unless toRefs is used.
computed creates cached derived values.
watchEffect runs side effects, like fetching or logging, when dependencies change.
Derived data belongs in computed; watchers are for side effects.

notEnough: Only saying both react to changes.

groups.title: Composition API Patterns
groups.question: Several components repeat the same fetching logic, and a listener keeps running after a component is removed. Explain composables and lifecycle hooks.

followUps.Composables for Logic Reuse: Why are composables better than mixins for reusing logic?
followUps.Lifecycle Hooks in Composition API: Where must lifecycle hooks be called?

evidence.text: A composable is a function that uses Vue's reactivity to hold logic.
Its return values make data flow explicit.
Unlike mixins, it avoids hidden name collisions.
Hooks like onMounted must be called synchronously during setup.
Inside async callbacks or after an await they may not register correctly.
onUnmounted cleans up listeners and timers.

groups.title: Vue Component Architecture
groups.question: A child component edits its props directly and a list component should let parents decide how each row looks. Explain props, emits and slots.

followUps.Props and Emits Contract: Why shouldn't a component change its props?
followUps.Slots and Render Scoping: How do scoped slots let a parent customise each row?

evidence.text: Props flow from parent to child.
A child tells the parent about changes by emitting events.
The parent owns the data and decides how to update it.
Slots let a parent pass template content into a child.
Scoped slots expose the child's data, like each row, to that template.
The child handles the logic while the parent controls the markup.

groups.title: Vite Build Tooling
groups.question: Edits sometimes reset component state during development, and an API key you set is undefined in the browser. Explain how Vite handles HMR and environment variables.

followUps.HMR and Dev Server Architecture: How does HMR update the page, and when does state reset?
followUps.Environment Variables and Modes: Why is a variable without the VITE_ prefix undefined in the browser?

evidence.text: Vite serves native ES modules during development.
HMR replaces only the changed module without a full reload.
Some changes cannot be patched in place, so the module reloads and its state resets.
Only variables with the VITE_ prefix are exposed to client code.
This stops secrets from leaking into the bundle by accident.
Anything exposed to the client can be read by users.
